title: Prove an exponential cost for resolving unpruned potential ancestry
statement: At K=2,alpha1=alpha2=1/2,r=1,fitness(S,0), the UNPRUNED unresolved count has b_n=Sn/2,d_n=n^2/2. Exact E_1 T=2 sum_(k>=0) S^k/[(k+1)^2 k!]=2e^S E[(Z+1)^-2],Z~Pois(S). Jensen gives E_1 T>=2e^S/(S+1)^2. Since at least one potential ancestor persists until absorption, expected selection births>=S E_1T/2>=S e^S/(S+1)^2. Full unpruned resolution therefore has exponential time/event cost. This does not lower-bound actual diffusion mixing, pruned/type-resolved graphs, other representations or the original whole-observation task. It is a precise mechanism obstruction; the unrestricted polynomial-selection endpoint remains open.
